subject: Greenfield Therapeutics — Pod sizing & quantization tradeoffs for 64k workloads
messages:
From: Evan Li <evan.li@greenfieldtx.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Connor <sasha.connor@greenfieldtx.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity for long-context workflows (64k) — sizing ask

Monica — thanks for the quick intro last week. We're moving from a research pilot into a product build and need a committed dedicated footprint for inference. High level:
- Primary model: fine-tuned open-architecture ~70B (we shared a model spec in the CSV).
- Target peak: ~120 requests/sec (burst to 180 for short windows).
- Typical token profile: median request ~1.2k tokens, but ~32% of traffic requires long retrieval/context stitches up to 64k tokens. Average response tokens ~700.
- Latency SLO: 300–600ms P95 for interactive flows (lower is better).
- Must evaluate quantization options — cost sensitive but cannot accept more than small, measurable quality drops.

Can you provide a recommended dedicated pod sizing (GPU type, number, memory headroom), quantization guidance (FP16 vs INT8 variants), and a proposed pilot plan? We'd like a committed proposal and cost estimate for procurement.

Attaching our traffic sample CSV. Happy to hop on a deep-dive with engineers.

— Evan
Evan Li
Director, ML Platform
Greenfield Therapeutics

Evan — thanks, received the CSV. Looping in Marcus and Karthik to own the detailed sizing. Quick clarifying questions to speed the sizing:
- Is the 70B model parameter count fixed (no further growth) or do you expect variants (65B/33B) for fallbacks?
- Distribution of token lengths: can you confirm the breakdown (you noted ~32% up to 64k — what % are >32k vs 64k exactly)?
- Any hard constraints on model precision (e.g., must be FP16 for validation) or are you open to INT8 / GPTQ style quant?

We'll produce: 1) memory per-session matrix (32k/64k) by quant level, 2) throughput per-GPU assumptions with realistic batching + KV caching behavior, 3) recommended durable commit (pods + spare) and pilot plan for quality/regression validation.

I'll draft a proposal and attach an initial capacity matrix by EOD tomorrow.

— Monica

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Li <evan.li@greenfieldtx.com>, Prio m Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for long-context workflows (64k) — sizing ask

Evan / team — took the CSV and ran a conservative sizing exercise. Summary up front: INT8 (post-GPTQ) yields ~2.5–3x reduction in model + KV footprint vs FP16, but requires careful evals for your retrieval/QA thresholds. For committed capacity with your 120 RPS peak and 32% long-context usage, recommended starting point = 18 H100-80GB GPUs (INT8+KV caching) or 34 A100-80GB GPUs (FP16) to hit latency SLO with headroom; details below.

Assumptions:
- Model baseline: 70B parameters, FP16 params ~35–38 GB resident (after optimizer/offload not considered for inference).
- KV cache: approximate growth = 0.6–0.9 bytes per token per KV slot aggregated; practical measured footprint ~0.45 GB per 1k tokens for this architecture in our runtime (includes layer keys+values, caching overhead).
- Effective session memory = model weights + peak KV cache + transient activation/batch buffers (~8–12% overhead).
- Batch strategy: continuous batching tuned for 30–80ms queueing; we assume average batch sizes that keep P95 under 600ms.

Memory matrix (approx):
- FP16 (no quant):
  - Model weights: 36 GB
  - KV for 32k context: 32k * 0.45 GB/1k = ~14.4 GB
  - KV for 64k context: ~28.8 GB
  - Total runtime working set (32k): ~36 + 14.4 + 6 (buffers) = ~56.4 GB -> fits on 80 GB headroom per GPU (A100/H100)
  - Total runtime (64k): ~36 + 28.8 + 6 = ~70.8 GB -> tight but fits on 80 GB with small headroom for spikes
- INT8 (post-quant / GPTQ style):
  - Model weights: ~14–16 GB (effective; depends on quant layout and extra dequant buffers)
  - KV cache remains mostly unchanged in size (quantization doesn't reduce KV footprint significantly for our runtime unless we also quantize KV entries) – assume same 0.45 GB/1k tokens
  - Totals: 32k -> ~14.5 + 14.4 + 5 = ~33.9 GB; 64k -> ~14.5 + 28.8 + 5 = ~48.3 GB

Throughput and pod sizing (P95 target ~500ms):
- Measured tokens/sec per GPU (interactive mix):
  - H100-80GB (INT8 runtime, optimized kernels + KV caching): ~25–40k tokens/s (depends on batch mixing)
  - A100-80GB (FP16): ~12–20k tokens/s
- Convert to RPS using your average tokens/request (~1.9k tokens/request including response):
  - H100 INT8: 25k–40k tps -> 13–21 RPS per GPU (conservative 15 RPS)
  - A100 FP16: 12–20k tps -> 6–10 RPS per GPU (conservative 7 RPS)

Sizing to 120 RPS (with 1.5x headroom for bursts + maintenance):
- INT8 on H100: required GPUs = ceil(120 / 15 * 1.5) = ~18 GPUs (we propose 20 reserved to be safe)
- FP16 on A100: required GPUs = ceil(120 / 7 * 1.5) = ~34 GPUs (we propose 36 reserved)

Operational recommendations:
- Pilot: 6 H100 GPUs (INT8) for a 2-week production pilot with shadow traffic and A/B quality checks against an FP16 baseline. We'll run automatic regen/QA scoring (you'll provide prompt set).
- Rollout: Start with 20 H100 reserved (INT8), keep 2–3 hot spares for maintenance, autoscale policy to burst onto shared capacity if needed.
- Fallbacks: deploy a smaller FP16 variant (33B) as a low-cost fallback for deep tails if quality regressions appear under quantization.

Risks / notes:
- INT8 quality varies by operator and prompt; we should gate commit on a quant-eval: blocked examples <1% change in your scoring metrics.
- KV cache dominates memory at 64k — quantization helps model weight memory but not KV unless we quantize cached KV (additional engineering effort).

I've attached a simple memory_matrix_64k.xlsx with per-session numbers and a rough 12/24-month GPU commit cost at current list. Monica — attaching the proposal PDF for customer-facing formatting.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Marcus — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple follow-ups:
1) What is the expected model-quality delta you typically see with INT8 for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) + your fine-tuning style? Can you share example evals or a short AB test?
2) Pricing: can you put the 20 H100 reserved and 36 A100 reserved numbers into a clean procurement worksheet so procurement can compare TCO?
3) Pilot: agree on the 2-week pilot. We'll provide a 50–100 prompt regression set and run blind quality evaluations.

If INT8 shows sub-1% regression on our metrics, procurement will prefer the INT8 commit. Please add the pilot statement and acceptance criteria to the proposal.

— Evan

Evan — great, we'll update the proposal:
- Add an explicit pilot scope: 2-week INT8 pilot on 6 H100 with shadow traffic + blind AB evaluation on your 100-prompt set; acceptance = <=1% delta on your primary metric and no more than 2% regression on secondary metrics.
- Procurement worksheet: we'll attach a TCO tab comparing 12/24 month commits for 20 H100 (INT8 baseline) vs 36 A100 (FP16 baseline) and show expected monthly token/unit costs.
- Next steps: I'll share the revised redwood_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf and memory_matrix_64k.xlsx (attached) by EOD. Marcus/Pre-sales to own pilot runbook and quality harness.

Target SLA sign date: 2027-06-10 (tentative) — Monica will coordinate an internal kickoff and a signature-ready package for procurement.
